description: Binds each materialized copy of Gridbook's PACKAGED runtime contract to the exact release it was taken from. The contract JSON is the sanctioned crossing of the repository boundary (AGENTS.md:38 -- 'compatibility crosses the repository boundary only through the immutable pin and contract'); the Gridbook RUNTIME is never vendored and never imported. Copies here are byte-verbatim: tests/test_gridbook_runtime_contract.py asserts each one equals the file inside the installed wheel, so a drifted copy fails the pinned-compatibility CI job rather than quietly attesting the wrong release.

contracts.lane_eligibility_detail: Gridbook 0.9.1 packages a lane-eligibility table at schema gridbook.lane-eligibility.v3 -- the first pinned release that does. Sixteen platform-scoped cells: two FP8-CB on sm_89 and ten CB on sm_120, every one of them qualification 'compile_only' (the kernels cross-compile for that capability; no device has been seen to take the route), plus four 'device_qualified' dense trellis cells on sm_121 from the 2026-08-29 GB10 receipt. A v3 cell is scoped to one platform, one payload family and an explicit rung list, and the table carries NO 'unbacked' cell: the runtime does not enumerate what it refuses, so ABSENCE is its only negative signal and an uncovered unit resolves UNATTESTED. CONSEQUENCE PrismaQuant must not paper over: sm_121 carries no CB cell at all. Both CB preflights hardcode their capability (sm89_preflight.SM89_CAPABILITY = (8, 9), sm120_preflight.SM120_CAPABILITY = (12, 0)), so no CB receipt for compute 12.1 exists to publish, and a CB export declaring target_platform sm_121 refuses at the route-status gate until Gridbook receipts one or the artifact declares a non-native target. That refusal is the table honestly reporting a serving gap (principle 1's carve-out, principle 9), not a gate defect. This entry replaces the 'absent' claim that held from 0.8.10 through 0.8.11 and the local proposal in docs/design/gridbook_lane_eligibility_contract.md, which the published v3 supersedes.

Gridbook 0.8.11 packages NO lane-eligibility table; its runtime_contract.json is byte-identical to 0.8.10's (sha256 0e2c32f3...), so everything said of 0.8.10 below holds unchanged. 0.8.11 is 0.8.10 plus two CUDA-graph capture fixes (gridbook#46 MXFP8 A-side offset pre-warm; gridbook#47 capture-safe padded grouped routing) -- neither changes what the contract publishes, and neither can be read from it. For 0.8.10 as for 0.8.11: Its contract publishes schema, contract_version, abi_features, quant_method, packing, layout, formats and producer_profiles, and gridbook/runtime_contract.py::validate_runtime_contract enforces that exact top-level key set -- so a 'lane_eligibility' block is not merely missing, it is currently REJECTED by the runtime's own validator. Nothing in the published fields determines which serving lane a unit's bytes ride: the persistent-B role-split refusal, the fused mid-M k%4 TMA law, the token-count regime thresholds and the operator serve flags all live in Gridbook source that the contract does not summarize. PrismaQuant therefore reports route status as UNATTESTED for this pin rather than transcribing those behaviours into local constants (principle 14: derived, or refused). docs/design/gridbook_lane_eligibility_contract.md is the exact table Gridbook must package to close this.
